quote_text:
Thanks for your patience, guys. Thank you, Phil.  Can you? Anything but. Phil, whenever you are  
ready, mate. Regis, what are your main emotions  at the moment? Proud, I think. Proud of the lads,  
proud of the atmosphere in the stadium, the  connection we had once again today to create  
something special. We had to win and I think we  were really focused on the way we wanted to play  
this game, showed good control, scored when it was  on, and finally the last part of the game was well  
managed with maturity. What does this rank for you  personally in your managerial career? At the top,  
top, top. Yeah, yeah. It's different. Wembley  was absolutely fantastic as well. It's a special  
place in English football and here today  it's the continuity of our journey. And  
the journey is really special because we feel the  alignment in the club with our fans and finally  
it's a tribute to our collective work and it's  really nice. We spoke about Trai the other day  
and he has been playing on the right wing and you  talked about his defensive contributions and that  
he could offer something in the final third, but  I'm not sure you saw a first-time volley. It's  
good. It's really nice to have this conversation  one week ago and then it's gone. Yeah. So often we  
try to analyse the game or the players just with  a technical lens, but it's more than that. It's  
about connection, hard work, connection between  players and balance. And Trai is a good example of  
a really good player, strong team-mate, always  working hard for the team, and then after that you  
have an emergence which today feels really good.  And Luke O'Nien had a big part of the work today.  
Yeah, it's good for them. And because they are  so well connected with the identity of the club,  
they set the tone and they helped the new lads  when they came into the club to understand what  
was our identity and they were really important.  How does the Europa League make you feel? Nervous,  
excited, calm? It's hard to realise, to be fair,  at the minute. It's going to be a new challenge,  
but we don't want to set a limit before. We know  that it's going to be tough in the Premier League,  
first of all, because the second season is hard as  well. So let's start with this idea, to be strong  
in the Premier League, and after that we'll have  the Europa League, which is another challenge,  
another story. We'll see. You've always said the  club hadn't been planning specifically for Europe,  
but are you confident in work that's gone on  to now enable you to start doing what needs  
to be done? Because you'll need a bigger squad,  deeper squad. Yes. A bit early to anticipate what  
will happen during the summer, but it's clear that  we are well aligned. We didn't want to anticipate  
the result of the season. Now it's done. We have  a good structure for the recruitment process and  
we'll work hard as usual, and I hope the new lads  and this team already will be well connected for  
the new season. What are the scenes like in  the dressing room? I think they are happy,  
really happy, and probably a bit tired  because it was hot, the stadium today,  
and probably from an emotion point of view as  well. They gave a lot. They were really well  
involved during the week, they worked hard and  they deserve to enjoy now. What are your plans  
to celebrate tonight? I don't know yet. I don't  know. It's going to be. We'll see. We'll see.  
When did you honestly start to think that European  qualification might be possible? Really late,  
to be fair, during the added time, because before  we were just focused on our game. It was a tough  
game, especially at 2-1, and Granit came just  near the dugout asking what was the situation. I  
didn't know before Proccie told me, "Okay, we are  seventh." Oh, yes. Really? Okay, just one minute  
to go. Let's push until the end. What does this  mean for Sunderland as it goes forward? I think  
it's an important step and it shows that anything  is possible in football, especially when you are  
working hard, you are representing the community,  you are humble. We struggled at times this season,  
had a really painful defeat here at home, and  they bounced back, they worked hard, and finally  
here is the result. So it's very positive. And  what does the next week or two look like for you  
now in terms of plans? I imagine you'll have  to sit down pretty quickly and kind of decide  
the next steps. Yes, probably, but let's wait 24  hours and we'll see. What does being in Europe  
mean for the entire city, not just the football  club? Because the club is such a kind of beacon  
for the whole town and it's been redeveloped  and regenerated. How important is Europe? Yeah,  
we feel the dynamic of the club. We are growing  fast, but the structure underneath is strong. And  
we can't say that it's perfect, but we feel  that we are improving a lot. So after that  
it's going to be an impulse for the future. And  I repeat, we have to stay humble because football  
is relentless, especially at that level. The  Premier League, first of all, and Europa League,  
obviously, so it's going to be new challenges  ahead, but we don't want to set the limit before.  
Just work hard like we did before and see. You're  quite a calm person yourself, Regis. Just when you  
take stock of this last year, it's one year to the  day since Wembley and now you've completed, you've  
got to the Europa League. Just what are those  emotions like, but also does it kind of surprise  
you as well how quickly the club has grown in  that space of time? Yeah, we are growing quickly,  
but in football it's hard to anticipate something.  We generated momentum. The players were so well  
connected, demanding with each other as well,  which is really important. We have great leaders  
in the group, young lads with the willingness  to learn. Just enjoy at the moment because in  
football it can go one way or the other way. At  the minute, everything is really well aligned.  
Keep going. I mean, it's been so surprising for  some people, maybe outside of the club, because  
you were written off essentially at the start of  the season by some places which suggested that  
you were going to be relegated. Has that kind of  underdog mentality really helped you this season?  
Yeah, it's important they stayed humble. And it's  another point about the data and predictions. You  
can't assess the connection between the players.  You can't assess the human relationship inside a  
group. And this group was absolutely outstanding.  What are you most looking forward to now with this  
group of players? I think we are looking forward  to the next ambition and on the pitch in their  
standards. I think we are feeling that the club is  growing and it's good to be part of that process.  
Was part of you annoyed last summer because you  were quite patronised and everyone expected you  
to really struggle and be relegated? Did that  sort of bring a defiance in you, in the place?  
Early in the season, I think it was obvious that  could have been hard and expected like this,  
but I didn't feel it in the dressing room any  time. It was clear that they were ambitious,  
humble but ambitious, and it's going to be the  same. So we know that, I repeat, it could be one  
way or the other way, it's always fragile, but  if you work hard and we have talented players,  
anything can happen. And has it quite suited  you that you've gone under the radar? I mean,  
in the north east alone, all the attention has  really been on Newcastle. So, yeah, it's good.  
Let's stay under the radar and I think it's the  best position and I think we'll stay like this.  
Regis, over the last few months and weeks, plenty  of us in this room have asked you about Europe,  
and every time you sort of batted that question  away. How sick were you of us asking, first of  
all, and how do you feel now? Yes, good. Even  hard to realise, to be fair, because for us in  
the club, it's a process and we trust the process.  Work hard, keep the same routine, more or less,  
trying to improve our process, but keep the  same routine. And with talent, with hard work,  
something can happen and it was the case. So we  don't need to change the attitudes. We still need  
to improve our way of working, but the attitudes  have to be the same. You just mentioned Xhaka.  
From the moment you signed him, did you think he  would have this sort of influence on the club?  
Yeah, it's impressive. He's a great player, first  of all, because the way he plays on the pitch,  
it's brilliant for a team. Composure, always  smart, with the belief that we can press and adapt  
in real time, and he's a great leader as well. So  he sets the standards every day. And it's not only  
by the voice, it's by the example. And yeah, his  influence has been massive. It's clear. Just one  
quick. So you didn't know that you were seventh  until what time? Were you not following the  
results? We had 10 minutes of added time. After  five minutes, so the last five minutes. Did you  
know what? I didn't know anything about the other  results. It was just about Sunderland against  
Chelsea. You started the season by beating West  Ham here in a great scene and you finish it like  
this. Those are two great moments and memories  for you. Yeah, absolutely. Absolutely. I think  
today we showed a great level of maturity and from  a performance point of view, I'm really proud of  
the way we delivered today. Good control on  the ball, the way we managed their press,  
created chances. We damaged their left side at the  beginning and obviously we had to manage different  
problems out of position, but I think the lads  did well. So I really appreciate the maturity of  
the group and it's exactly the direction we want  to take. Great. Cheers, guys. Thank you so much.
title: LE BRIS: “LET’S STAY UNDER THE RADAR!”  Sunderland 2-1 Chelsea
